title: Research Design Fundamentals
summary: Plan a sound study, from a clear research question to a workable analysis plan.
description:
This course takes participants through the decisions that shape a credible study: framing research questions, choosing a design, defining variables, planning sampling and data collection, and writing an analysis plan before any data is collected.

Sessions combine short explanations with group work on participants' own projects.
outcomes: Write focused research questions and objectives
Choose an appropriate study design
Plan sampling, data collection and analysis
Recognise common threats to validity
audience: Postgraduate students, early-career researchers and programme staff starting a study.

title: Questionnaire Design and Survey Methods
summary: Write questions people can answer accurately and run a survey that produces usable data.
description:
Participants learn how to turn objectives into measurable questions, write clear and neutral wording, choose answer formats and scales, structure a questionnaire, and pilot it. The course also covers sampling basics, online and face-to-face collection, and data quality checks.

Participants build and test a questionnaire in Afrimetrica Surveys during the course.
outcomes: Translate objectives into measurable questions
Avoid leading, double-barrelled and vague questions
Choose suitable scales, including Likert scales
Pilot a questionnaire and check data quality
audience: Anyone who designs or commissions surveys.

title: Sampling and Sample Size
summary: Choose a sampling approach and calculate how many responses you really need.
description: The course covers probability and non-probability sampling, stratification and clustering, sampling frames, margin of error and confidence, sample size for subgroups, and adjusting for response rates and design effects.
outcomes: Choose an appropriate sampling strategy
Calculate sample sizes for common designs
Account for non-response and design effects
Explain sampling limitations honestly in reports
audience: Researchers, evaluators and analysts planning surveys.

title: Quantitative Data Analysis with SPSS, Stata or R
summary: Clean, analyse and interpret survey and research data with a statistical package.
description: Hands-on sessions cover data cleaning, descriptive statistics, cross-tabulation and chi-square tests, t-tests and ANOVA, correlation and linear regression, and an introduction to logistic regression. Participants work with real datasets and learn to report results clearly.
outcomes: Prepare and clean a dataset for analysis
Choose and run appropriate statistical tests
Interpret and report results correctly
Produce tables and charts for reports
audience: Researchers and analysts with basic statistics knowledge.

title: Qualitative Research and Thematic Analysis
summary: Plan interviews and focus groups and analyse what people say rigorously.
description: The course covers qualitative designs, interview and focus group guides, facilitation, transcription, coding and thematic analysis, and how to report qualitative findings credibly.
outcomes: Design interview and focus group guides
Facilitate discussions that produce rich data
Code transcripts and develop themes
Report qualitative findings with appropriate evidence
audience: Researchers, evaluators and students using qualitative methods.

title: Monitoring and Evaluation for Programmes
summary: Build a practical M&E framework, indicators and data system for a programme.
description: Participants develop a theory of change and results framework, define indicators, plan baselines and data collection, and design reporting and learning processes. The course also introduces common evaluation designs and how to commission an evaluation.
outcomes: Develop a theory of change and results framework
Write measurable indicators with targets
Plan baseline, monitoring and evaluation data
Use M&E findings for decisions and learning
audience: Programme managers, M&E officers and NGO staff.

title: Research Ethics and Data Protection
summary: Protect participants and their data from consent to archiving.
description: The course covers informed consent, confidentiality and anonymisation, working with vulnerable groups, ethics review, and handling personal data responsibly, including the principles of Ghana's Data Protection Act and good practice for storing and sharing research data.
outcomes: Design informed consent processes
Anonymise and protect personal data
Prepare for ethics review
Plan secure storage, retention and sharing
audience: Researchers, students and data collection teams.

title: Data Visualisation and Research Reporting
summary: Turn results into clear charts, summaries and reports that decision-makers use.
description: Participants learn to choose the right chart, design clean tables, write findings and recommendations in plain language, and structure reports and briefs for different audiences.
outcomes: Choose effective charts for different data
Write clear findings and recommendations
Structure reports and policy briefs
Present results to non-specialists
